question.text: If the quadratic equation $a x^2+b x+c=0(a\gt0)$ has two roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that $\alpha \lt -2$ and $\beta\gt2$ then

solution.text: Hint: $f(x)=a x^2+b x+c$ so, $f(-2) \lt 0$ and $f(2)\gt0$ also, $f(0) \lt 0 \Rightarrow c \lt 0$ $\begin{aligned} & f(-1) \lt 0 \Rightarrow a-b+c \lt 0 \\ & f(1) \lt 0 \Rightarrow a+b+c \lt 0 \end{aligned}$
